title: Tamar and the Magnifying Glass
summary: In synagogue, Tamar hears that a kosher fish needs fins and scales, and a kosher animal needs split hooves and must chew its cud. So she sets out with a magnifying glass to check for herself. A funny, curious story about the Torah's signs of kosher animals.
pages:
On Shabbat, in the synagogue, Tamar listens to the Torah reading.
"Whatever has fins and scales... those you may eat."
Tamar raises an eyebrow. Scales? What are those?

"Abba," she asks on the way home, "how do you know which fish is kosher?"
"It needs fins to swim," says Abba, "and scales, like little coins all over its body."

On Sunday, Tamar takes a magnifying glass out of the drawer.
"I'm going to check for myself!" she announces.
Imma smiles. "Good luck, explorer."

At the market, at the fish seller's stall, there is a big silver fish.
Tamar comes closer with her magnifying glass.
"Fins: yes! Scales: yes, they're shiny! This fish is kosher!"

Next to the fish lies a pink, curly shrimp.
Tamar looks and looks.
"No fins, and no scales. Sorry, shrimp, you're not for us."

On Friday they drive to a farm.
"And an animal," Abba explains, "needs split hooves, which means a foot divided in two, and it has to chew its cud."

"Chew its cud?" Tamar laughs. "What's that?"
"The animal eats, and then it brings the food back up into its mouth and chews it all over again," says Abba.
"Yuck!" laughs Tamar. "But also kind of cool."

Tamar bends down next to a brown cow.
Magnifying glass on the foot: "Split hoof, yes!"
Magnifying glass on the mouth: chew, chew, chew. "Chewing its cud, yes!"

"Moooo," says the cow.
"Yes, yes," says Tamar, "you're kosher. Nothing to worry about."

Then along comes a tall camel, chewing lazily.
"You chew your cud," says Tamar, "but your foot isn't split all the way.
You're not kosher, but you're very handsome."

In the evening, Tamar draws a big chart.
A fish with fins and scales. A cow with hooves and a chewing mouth.
And at the top she writes: "Tamar's Lab."

"Abba," she says before bed, "the Torah gave us signs, and I know how to check them!"
So which animal will we check tomorrow?
